business_objectives: Make the `muse-spark` contributor tier usable only in repositories where the user has explicitly consented to it, so that no unattended develop/review run can ever send a project's diff to the contributor tier by accident.
Enforce that gate deterministically in code (a PreToolUse(Bash) hook), not by instruction text an LLM reviewer or a prompt-injected agent can be talked out of.
Keep every non-consented project's develop/review run behaving exactly as it does today: the contributor tier is simply unavailable, nothing new is asked, nothing halts.
Write the judgement that cannot be mechanized - when the contributor tier is outside the scope of a given consent - as pre-dispatch criteria in the review registry/protocol documents of both plugins.

functional_requirements.title: muse_guard.py PreToolUse(Bash) hook in both plugins
functional_requirements.statement: Add `muse_guard.py` under BOTH `em-workflow/hooks/` and `em-review/hooks/`, a PreToolUse(Bash) hook that decides on Bash commands invoking the `muse-spark-contributor` tier: deny when the current project has no recorded consent, no decision otherwise. It follows bash_guard.py's structure (stdin PreToolUse JSON, `hookSpecificOutput` on stdout, exit 0 always) and is code-only - no LLM, no network, no prompt. The two copies are byte-identical apart from anything that must name its own plugin; no shared module is extracted.

functional_requirements.title: Presence-only consent store
functional_requirements.statement: Consent is recorded in a user-owned JSON store outside any repository (`~/.claude/em-workflow/muse-consent.json`), shaped as `{version, projects: {<project key>: {updated_at}}}`. Both plugins' copies read and write this SAME path, so consent granted through either plugin applies to both. The presence of the project key IS the consent; no visibility, license, contributor-count or any other fact is stored. The store path is overridable with `$EM_WORKFLOW_MUSE_CONSENT` (tests only), mirroring `$EM_WORKFLOW_APPROVALS`.

functional_requirements.title: Project key identical to bash_guard's
functional_requirements.statement: The project key is derived exactly as `bash_guard.project_key`: `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` for the invocation cwd, falling back to `os.path.realpath(directory)` when git is unavailable or the directory is not a repository. Consequence: every worktree of the same repository (including `.claude/worktrees/...` integration and task worktrees) resolves to one consent entry, and a non-git directory still gets a stable key.

functional_requirements.title: Deny on unconsented contributor-tier invocation
functional_requirements.statement: When the command is a contributor-tier invocation and the project key is absent from the consent store, the hook emits `permissionDecision: deny` with a Japanese reason naming the missing consent and an `additionalContext` telling the agent to use the non-contributor `muse-spark` entry (or another chain entry) instead of seeking a workaround. The hook never emits `ask` and never emits `allow`.

functional_requirements.title: No misfire outside contributor-tier invocations
functional_requirements.statement: The hook produces no decision (exit 0, empty stdout) for: any command not invoking the contributor tier; a plain `muse-spark` invocation; and any command that merely MENTIONS `muse-spark-contributor` without invoking it - inside single/double quotes, as a `grep`/`rg` pattern argument, or inside a here-document body. Matching is boundary-aware in both directions: `muse-spark` must never be read as the contributor tier, and `muse-spark-contributor` must never be read as the plain tier (superstring boundary). Argument spellings that ARE invocations must be recognized in every form the harness uses: bare `-m muse-spark-contributor`, `--model=muse-spark-contributor`, and quoted equivalents.

functional_requirements.title: Store-absence and malformed-store handling
functional_requirements.statement: An absent store file, an unreadable store, invalid JSON, or a structurally unexpected store (not a dict, or `projects` not a dict) is all treated as 'no consent for any project' - a contributor-tier invocation is denied, everything else still gets no decision. The hook never creates, repairs, or writes the store; it is read-only at hook time.

functional_requirements.title: Consent-recording CLI
functional_requirements.statement: `muse_guard.py` provides the out-of-band CLI the user runs to grant or withdraw consent: `--record --project-dir DIR`, `--remove --project-dir DIR`, `--list --project-dir DIR`. `--record` writes `{updated_at}` for the derived project key; `--remove` deletes the key entirely; writes are atomic (temp file + `os.replace`) and create the parent directory as needed, mirroring bash_guard's CLI. Direct editing of the store with Write/Edit is prohibited; every mutation goes through this CLI. The CLI is never invoked by the hook path and never by the workflow itself.

functional_requirements.title: Hook registration in both plugins
functional_requirements.statement: Register the hook in `em-workflow/hooks/hooks.json` under the existing `PreToolUse` / matcher `Bash` group with the verbatim command form `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/muse_guard.py` and `timeout: 15`, placed before `destructive-guard.py` so its blanket allow never ends the decision first; update `EXPECTED_BASH_GUARD_ORDER` in `tests/test_guardrail_hooks_migration.py` accordingly. Create `em-review/hooks/hooks.json` - em-review's first hooks file - registering the same script in the same verbatim form with the same timeout. Both hooks firing for one Bash call is idempotent: they read the same store and return the same decision.

functional_requirements.title: Written pre-dispatch criteria for consent scope
functional_requirements.statement: Document in `em-workflow/references/reviewers.yaml` + `em-workflow/references/review-phase.md`, and in the `em-review` counterparts: (a) the read-mapping rule - when `muse-spark` is the selected chain entry, the contributor tier may be substituted only after two checks, whether this project's consent is recorded (mechanical) and whether this particular dispatch may use it (per-dispatch LLM judgement); (b) the explicit exception to review-phase.md's `never substitute a model of your own choosing` clause, pointing at that read-mapping rule and stating that the decision is made BEFORE dispatch; (c) exactly one per-dispatch 'do not use' item - a change whose core is an unpublished idea, i.e. a new feature whose design or approach is a differentiator for the project - kept textually distinct from (d) three 'outside the scope of consent' conditions: secrets in the diff (API keys, credentials, internal endpoints, customer data); third-party copyrighted content (vendored code, externally supplied patches, contributor PRs); and the repository being private or relicensed. The per-dispatch default is 'use'; it is not fail-closed, and security-perspective reviews are not excluded. Per the orchestrator's constraint on the `security.out-of-scope-enforcement` answer, the third out-of-scope condition MUST be written as a check of the CURRENT state at dispatch time - 'if the repository is currently private, or its license is no longer one the consent was reasonable under, do not use the contributor tier' - never as a comparison against a consent-time recorded value.

functional_requirements.title: Guard tests under the repository-root tests/ directory
functional_requirements.statement: Guard tests live at `tests/test_muse_guard.py` and run under the existing entry point `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, covering both the deny side and the no-misfire side, and exercising both plugins' copies of the script. No `hooks/tests/muse-guard-cases.json` and no `hooks/tests/run-muse-guard.py` are created - the destructive-guard case-runner pattern is NOT replicated for this hook.

functional_requirements.title: reviewers.yaml chain immutability
functional_requirements.statement: No `primary_chain` in either plugin's `references/reviewers.yaml` changes: the six perspectives keep their existing entries (`{harness: litellm, model: muse-spark}` stays exactly where it is today), and no `muse-spark-contributor` entry is ever added to a chain. The new prose goes where the file's restricted-parser test tolerates it (the header comment block or outside the `perspectives:` block) and must not introduce the literal string `cross_validation`. The contributor tier is opt-in at dispatch time under the FR9 criteria, not a registry-level default, so the per-perspective hop budget is unaffected.

functional_requirements.title: Version bump in both plugins
functional_requirements.statement: Because files under both `em-workflow/` and `em-review/` change, bump both plugins' versions in the same change, keeping each plugin's `<plugin>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` `version` equal to its entry in the repository-root `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (em-workflow from 0.1.69, em-review from 0.5.7), per `.claude/rules/core-plugin-version-bump.md`.

functional_requirements.title: contributor-consent skill in both plugins
functional_requirements.statement: Add `skills/contributor-consent/SKILL.md` to BOTH plugins. It is run manually by the user in an interactive session and is never invoked by develop. It first probes for the vertex-review LiteLLM harness using the `litellm_available` probe already defined in each plugin's review-phase.md, and exits with a plain 'not installed' message when the probe is false. Otherwise it mechanically gathers exactly three facts - remote visibility (`gh repo view --json visibility` or equivalent), the license, and whether the user is the only contributor - presents them, and takes consent through a single `AskUserQuestion` round, then records it via FR7's `--record`. It does not present whether unpushed commits exist. The same skill handles revocation via `--remove`. It never gathers judgement material conversationally. Per `.claude/rules/slash-commands-as-skills.md` it is a skill, never a `commands/` file.

non_functional_requirements.title: Deterministic, offline decision
non_functional_requirements.statement: The hook's decision is a pure function of the command string and the on-disk consent store. It performs no network access, no LLM call, and no repository-metadata fetch, preserving the existing no-network guard precedent for PreToolUse(Bash) hooks that fire on every Bash call.

non_functional_requirements.title: Fail open to the normal permission flow, never `ask`
non_functional_requirements.statement: Anything the hook cannot classify with confidence yields no decision (exit 0, no output) so the normal permission flow applies. The hook never emits `ask`, because `ask` is demoted to `deny` under `claude-batch` and would halt an unattended run with nobody to answer.

non_functional_requirements.title: Unattended-run safety
non_functional_requirements.statement: No new `AskUserQuestion` site is introduced in any develop-phase or review-phase document of either plugin. A develop run in a non-consented project proceeds exactly as today, minus the contributor tier; consent is granted only out-of-band via the FR13 skill and FR7's CLI. `--batch` gets no special case.

non_functional_requirements.title: Latency within the registered timeout
non_functional_requirements.statement: The hook completes far inside its `timeout: 15`: at most one `git` subprocess with a 5-second timeout (the FR3 key derivation) plus one small JSON read, and it short-circuits before both when the command is not a contributor-tier invocation.

non_functional_requirements.title: Test isolation from real user state
non_functional_requirements.statement: Tests never read or write real `~/.claude` state: they set `$EM_WORKFLOW_MUSE_CONSENT` to a path under `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` and invoke the hook as a subprocess with JSON on stdin, per `test/README.md`.

non_functional_requirements.title: No third-party test dependencies
non_functional_requirements.statement: Test code uses only the Python standard library (`unittest`, `json`, `subprocess`, `tempfile`), per `test/README.md`'s no-external-dependencies rule for tests.

non_functional_requirements.title: Consent store records nothing but presence
non_functional_requirements.statement: The store's per-project value carries `updated_at` and nothing else. No repository visibility, license identifier, contributor list, diff content, or path is ever written to it.

non_functional_requirements.title: Structural consistency with the existing guard family
non_functional_requirements.statement: Each registration passes the existing well-formedness invariants unchanged: the plugin-root-relative verbatim command shape, the per-script timeout table, no duplicate registration of the same script under one event, and the executable-bit / referenced-script-exists checks - applied to em-review's new hooks.json as well as em-workflow's.

non_functional_requirements.title: Duplicate-hook idempotency
non_functional_requirements.statement: When both plugins are installed, `muse_guard.py` fires twice for the same Bash call. Both copies read the same store and reach the same decision, so the duplicate is a no-op: two denies are equivalent to one, and two no-decisions leave the permission flow untouched.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: With an empty or absent consent store, a Bash command invoking the `muse-spark-contributor` tier receives `permissionDecision: deny` from `muse_guard.py`, and the same command receives no decision once that project's key is present in the store. This holds for both plugins' copies of the script.
With an empty or absent consent store, a plain `muse-spark` invocation receives NO decision from `muse_guard.py` (exit 0, empty stdout).
A command that merely mentions `muse-spark-contributor` inside quotes, as a grep/rg pattern, or inside a here-document body receives no decision.

An absent store, an invalid-JSON store, and a structurally unexpected store each behave as 'no consent': deny for a contributor-tier invocation, no decision otherwise. The store file is never created or modified by the hook path.

Two different worktrees of the same repository resolve to the same consent entry (consent recorded from one is honored in the other); a non-git directory falls back to its realpath key and is still deniable/consentable.

`em-workflow/hooks/hooks.json` registers `muse_guard.py` in the PreToolUse(Bash) group with the verbatim `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/muse_guard.py` form and `timeout: 15`, ordered before `destructive-guard.py`; `EXPECTED_BASH_GUARD_ORDER` includes it in exactly that position; `em-review/hooks/hooks.json` exists and registers the same script in the same verbatim form and timeout; every existing hooks-registration invariant still passes for both files.

Both plugins' `references/reviewers.yaml` and `references/review-phase.md` state the read-mapping rule, the substitute-prohibition exception with its pre-dispatch timing, the one per-dispatch 'do not use' item, and the three out-of-scope conditions - the one and the three kept textually distinct - with the visibility/license condition phrased as a check of the CURRENT state at dispatch time.

Every `primary_chain` entry in both plugins' `references/reviewers.yaml` is byte-for-byte unchanged from before this feature; no chain anywhere contains `muse-spark-contributor`; the literal string `cross_validation` is still absent from em-workflow's reviewers.yaml.
The develop-phase and review-phase documents of both plugins gain no new `AskUserQuestion` site relative to the base revision - verified mechanically, not by running develop.

`em-workflow` and `em-review` each carry the same version string in `<plugin>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and in the matching entry of `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, and both are higher than their base-revision values.
`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passes with `tests/test_muse_guard.py` present; no file is created under either plugin's `hooks/tests/` for this feature.

`skills/contributor-consent/SKILL.md` exists in both plugins and describes: the vertex-review/LiteLLM presence probe with its 'not installed' exit, the three presented facts, a single `AskUserQuestion` round, recording via `muse_guard.py --record`, and revocation via `--remove`. It does not present unpushed-commit status, and it is not referenced from any develop-phase document.

test_scenarios.title: Deny: contributor-tier invocation with an absent consent store
test_scenarios.given: $EM_WORKFLOW_MUSE_CONSENT points at a path inside a TemporaryDirectory that does not exist.
test_scenarios.when: muse_guard.py is invoked as a subprocess with PreToolUse JSON whose tool_name is Bash and whose tool_input.command invokes the contributor tier (e.g. `codex exec -p litellm -m muse-spark-contributor ...`), cwd set to a temporary git repository.
test_scenarios.then: exit code 0; stdout parses as JSON with hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName == 'PreToolUse' and permissionDecision == 'deny'; permissionDecisionReason names the missing consent; additionalContext directs the agent to a non-contributor entry. The store path still does not exist afterwards. Asserted against both plugins' copies of the script.

test_scenarios.title: Allowed through: contributor-tier invocation after consent is recorded
test_scenarios.given: The same temporary repository, with consent recorded via `muse_guard.py --record --project-dir <repo>`.
test_scenarios.when: The identical TS-1 payload is replayed.
test_scenarios.then: exit code 0 and empty stdout (no decision). The store contains exactly one project key whose value has an `updated_at` field and no other key. Consent recorded through one plugin's copy is honored by the other plugin's copy.

test_scenarios.title: No misfire: plain `muse-spark` is never treated as the contributor tier
test_scenarios.when: Commands invoking the plain tier are submitted: `codex exec -p litellm -m muse-spark`, `--model=muse-spark`, `-m "muse-spark"`.
test_scenarios.then: Each yields exit 0 and empty stdout.

test_scenarios.title: No misfire: contributor tier is never treated as the plain tier
test_scenarios.given: Consent store containing an unrelated project key only.
test_scenarios.when: `-m muse-spark-contributor` is submitted from a repository whose key is NOT in the store.
test_scenarios.then: deny - matching on the plain-tier substring must not cause the contributor invocation to slip through.

test_scenarios.title: Argument spelling variants of a real invocation
test_scenarios.when: Each spelling is submitted separately: `-m muse-spark-contributor`, `-m 'muse-spark-contributor'`, `-m "muse-spark-contributor"`, `--model=muse-spark-contributor`, `--model='muse-spark-contributor'`.

test_scenarios.title: No misfire: mentions that are not invocations
test_scenarios.when: Each of the following is submitted: `echo 'do not use muse-spark-contributor'`; `grep -n muse-spark-contributor em-workflow/references/reviewers.yaml`; `rg "muse-spark-contributor" .`; a here-document whose body contains the string; `git commit -m "docs: explain muse-spark-contributor consent"`.
test_scenarios.then: Each yields exit 0 and empty stdout.

test_scenarios.title: No misfire: unrelated commands and non-Bash tools
test_scenarios.when: Payloads are submitted for `git status`, `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, a payload with tool_name != 'Bash', a payload with an empty command, and unparseable stdin.
test_scenarios.then: Every case yields exit 0 and empty stdout.

test_scenarios.title: Malformed consent store is treated as no consent
test_scenarios.given: $EM_WORKFLOW_MUSE_CONSENT points at, in turn: a file containing `not json`; a file containing `[]`; a file containing `{"projects": "nope"}`; a directory instead of a file.
test_scenarios.when: A contributor-tier invocation, then a plain `muse-spark` invocation, are submitted for each store state.
test_scenarios.then: Contributor invocation denied in every case; plain invocation gets no decision in every case; the store file is never rewritten or repaired.

test_scenarios.title: Non-git realpath fallback
test_scenarios.given: A plain temporary directory that is not inside any git repository, reached through a symlink.
test_scenarios.when: `muse_guard.py --record --project-dir <symlinked path>` is run, then a contributor-tier invocation is submitted with cwd set to the real path (and separately to the symlinked path).
test_scenarios.then: The recorded key equals `os.path.realpath(dir)`, and both invocations resolve to that same key (no decision after recording, deny before).

test_scenarios.title: Worktree key identity
test_scenarios.given: A temporary git repository plus a `git worktree add`-created second worktree of it.
test_scenarios.when: Consent is recorded from the main worktree, then a contributor-tier invocation is submitted with cwd set to the linked worktree; and, in a second case, consent is removed and the same invocation is replayed from both worktrees.
test_scenarios.then: Both worktrees share one consent entry: no decision in both after recording, deny in both after `--remove`. The store never holds two keys for one repository.

test_scenarios.title: Consent CLI round trip
test_scenarios.given: A temporary store path and a temporary git repository.
test_scenarios.then: `--record` is idempotent (one key, `updated_at` refreshed); `--list` prints the project key when consented and nothing when not; `--remove` deletes the key entirely rather than leaving an empty object; the written JSON contains no field other than `version`, `projects`, the key, and `updated_at`.

test_scenarios.title: Hook registration invariants in both plugins
test_scenarios.when: Each PreToolUse/Bash group's script filenames are extracted and each entry is checked against the existing well-formedness rules.
test_scenarios.then: em-workflow's extracted list equals `EXPECTED_BASH_GUARD_ORDER` including `muse_guard.py`, whose index is less than `destructive-guard.py`'s, with `destructive-guard.py` still last; em-review's file registers `muse_guard.py` under PreToolUse matcher Bash; both entries' command is exactly `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/muse_guard.py` with `timeout` 15; both referenced scripts exist and are executable; no script is registered twice under one event in either file.

test_scenarios.title: reviewers.yaml chain immutability
test_scenarios.when: Every perspective's `primary_chain` is parsed and compared against the expected literal chain list, and every chain entry's `model` value is checked.
test_scenarios.then: Each perspective's chain matches its expected list exactly; no `model` value anywhere equals `muse-spark-contributor`; every perspective still has a non-empty chain; the literal string `cross_validation` is still absent from em-workflow's reviewers.yaml.

test_scenarios.title: Documented criteria: read-mapping, substitute exception, one-vs-three split, current-state drift
test_scenarios.when: The consent section is located in each file and its text asserted.
test_scenarios.then: Each pair names the consent precondition and the two-check read-mapping rule; review-phase.md records the exception to `never substitute a model of your own choosing` and states the decision is made before dispatch; the one per-dispatch 'do not use' item and the three out-of-scope conditions appear as textually distinct groups; the visibility/license condition is expressed as a check of the current state at dispatch time and contains no comparison against a consent-time recorded value.

test_scenarios.title: No new AskUserQuestion site (develop-run static equivalent)
test_scenarios.given: The develop-phase and review-phase documents of both plugins.
test_scenarios.when: Occurrences of `AskUserQuestion` are counted per file and compared against the expected per-file counts pinned by this feature.
test_scenarios.then: No file's count increased; the consent feature introduces no interactive gate anywhere in the develop or review path. The `contributor-consent` skill's own AskUserQuestion is outside this set and is not referenced from any develop-phase document.

test_scenarios.title: Plugin version bump consistency
test_scenarios.when: Each plugin's `version` is compared with its marketplace entry's `version`.
test_scenarios.then: Both pairs are equal; each version parses as semver; em-workflow > 0.1.69 and em-review > 0.5.7.

test_scenarios.title: Test placement conforms to the repository convention
test_scenarios.when: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` is run and the tree is checked.
test_scenarios.then: The suite passes with `tests/test_muse_guard.py` collected; neither plugin's `hooks/tests/` contains a muse-guard case file or runner; the guard tests import no third-party package.

test_scenarios.title: contributor-consent skill shape
test_scenarios.when: Each file's frontmatter and body are asserted.
test_scenarios.then: Both exist with valid skill frontmatter; each describes the LiteLLM/vertex-review presence probe and its 'not installed' exit, the three presented facts (remote visibility, license, sole contributor), exactly one AskUserQuestion round, recording via `muse_guard.py --record` and revocation via `--remove`; neither mentions unpushed commits as a presented fact; neither is referenced from any develop-phase document; no `commands/` file is added for it.

assumptions.statement: The consent store lives outside every repository, at `~/.claude/em-workflow/muse-consent.json`, mirroring bash_guard.py's approvals.json placement, and both plugins' copies use that same path.
assumptions.rationale: A store inside the repository would let a cloned repo ship someone else's consent; the approval store already establishes the user-owned-location precedent. A per-plugin path would make consent granted in one plugin invisible to the other.

assumptions.statement: The project key is derived exactly as `bash_guard.project_key` (git-common-dir, realpath fallback), so consent is per repository and shared by all of its worktrees.
assumptions.rationale: The whole workflow runs inside per-feature integration and per-task worktrees; a per-directory key would silently un-consent every worktree.

assumptions.statement: The guard emits only `deny` or no decision - never `ask`, never `allow`.
assumptions.rationale: `ask` is demoted to `deny` under claude-batch with nobody to answer, and an explicit `allow` would override later guards in the chain that must still get their say.

assumptions.statement: The store path is overridable with `$EM_WORKFLOW_MUSE_CONSENT`, and the tests use it exclusively.
assumptions.rationale: test/README.md requires environment-variable overrides for state isolation and forbids touching real `~/.claude` state from tests; `$EM_WORKFLOW_APPROVALS` is the existing precedent.

assumptions.statement: The hook registers in em-workflow's existing PreToolUse(Bash) group with `timeout: 15`, before `destructive-guard.py`, and in a new em-review hooks.json with the same form and timeout.
assumptions.rationale: 15 is the standard timeout in the per-script timeout table, and destructive-guard.py's blanket allow must run last so it never ends the decision before this guard is consulted.

assumptions.statement: muse_guard.py is duplicated verbatim into BOTH plugins' `hooks/` directories; em-review gains its first `hooks/hooks.json`. No shared module is extracted.
assumptions.rationale: Gate resolution of `create-spec.em-review-hook-parity` -> `both_plugins_ship_the_hook` (Codex-consulted). Shipping the hook only in em-workflow leaves a user who installs em-review alone with no mechanical enforcement at all - an environment-dependent security gap, since em-review's own review phase dispatches the same `codex exec -p litellm -m <model>` invocation. The hook is a silent no-op for every non-contributor command, so adding a hooks surface to em-review changes nothing observable in ordinary use, and the duplicate is idempotent because both copies read the same store. `shared/` extraction is explicitly out of scope for this task.

assumptions.statement: No `primary_chain` gains a `muse-spark-contributor` entry; the contributor tier is selected at dispatch time under the written criteria, never by the registry.
assumptions.rationale: Putting it in a chain would make it the automatic first hop for some perspective, which is exactly what consent is meant to prevent; chain immutability is asserted by tests, and keeping the entry count fixed leaves the per-perspective hop budget untouched.

assumptions.statement: Guard tests go in the repository-root `tests/` directory as `tests/test_muse_guard.py`, run by `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`; no `hooks/tests/muse-guard-cases.json` and no `run-muse-guard.py` are created.
assumptions.rationale: Gate resolution of `testing.muse-guard-test-location` -> `repo_root_unittest` (Codex-consulted, recorded per batch policy `record_as_assumption`). `test/README.md` is the repository's test-convention SSOT and every other hook is already tested from `tests/`, so a `hooks/tests/` runner would never run under the standard entry point. The task description's `hooks/tests/` wording is reconciled downward to the SSOT.

assumptions.statement: The 'run develop in a non-consented project' criterion is discharged by automated static-equivalent tests, not by a real develop run.
assumptions.rationale: Gate resolution of `acceptance.develop-smoke-verification` -> `static_equivalent_tests` (Codex-consulted, recorded per batch policy `record_as_assumption`). This specification is produced inside an unattended batch run of that same develop workflow, so a manual verify step requiring a human can never be discharged; the repository has no e2e harness; the static equivalents capture the criterion's intent and run under the standard entry point.

assumptions.statement: The three 'outside the scope of consent' conditions stay written pre-dispatch criteria in `references/reviewers.yaml` and `references/review-phase.md`, applied by the LLM before dispatch; `muse_guard.py` checks consent presence only, the store keeps its presence-only shape, no visibility/license/contributor facts are recorded, and the guard performs no network access. The written criteria state the drift condition as a check of the CURRENT state at dispatch time.
assumptions.rationale: Gate resolution of `security.out-of-scope-enforcement` -> `documented_only`, with the orchestrator's attached current-state constraint (Codex-consulted). A network fetch inside a PreToolUse(Bash) hook firing on every Bash call under a 15-second timeout would false-positive on a transient failure and halt an unattended run; widening the store schema adds fragile sole-contributor tracking for a condition that reduces to a current-state check, while secrets-in-diff and third-party content are inherently per-diff judgements that cannot be captured at consent time.

assumptions.statement: The `design` step runs for this feature (`status: pending`).
assumptions.rationale: Gate resolution of `design-step.recommendation` -> `decide_autonomously` (references/batch-policies.yaml); the analyst's recommendation was adopted without asking the user, because the change settles the store shape, the command-matching algorithm, the PreToolUse ordering and the reviewers.yaml placement constraint together.
